openDecisions.question: Does the statistics contract evolve additively (every new key optional, flat topOrders kept), or does it break, forcing hand edits in apps/web?
openDecisions.specOffers: backend/08_top_orders_by_currency.md:9 says "Replace/deprecate global topOrders". backend/16_shared_contracts_and_openapi.md:36-40 leaves the choice open between evolving the existing schema directly and introducing a v2 shape, and says direct evolution is acceptable "if all callers migrate in same change".
openDecisions.codebaseMakesCheaper: Additive is dramatically cheaper. Three hand-written apps/web files consume the contract by type: apps/web/src/features/delivery/model/statistics-view-model.ts:1-7 imports BookOrderStatisticsView and BookOrderStatisticsTopOrder straight from @app/shared and reads view.topOrders at :142; apps/web/src/features/delivery/components/delivery-history.fixtures.ts:123 declares `export const statisticsViewFixture: BookOrderStatisticsView = {...}` as an explicitly typed object literal, so ANY new required key breaks root pnpm typecheck there; apps/web/src/features/delivery/api/use-statistics.ts:14 runs BookOrderStatisticsViewSchema.parse at runtime, so extra keys the FE does not declare are silently stripped rather than crashing. The pre-push hook runs pnpm typecheck across all packages, so a breaking change cannot be pushed without FE edits that are outside the stated scope.
options: A. Fully additive: every new top-level key (meta, comparison, lifecycle, costs, landedCost, topOrdersByCurrency, pulse, daily, records) is .optional() in BookOrderStatisticsViewSchema, and the flat topOrders array stays as a deprecated alias populated from the UAH-or-first-currency group. Zero apps/web edits. Cost: nine optional keys the backend always populates, which is exactly the nullable/optional ambiguity backend/16:32 warns against.

B. Additive-required with one FE fixture edit: new keys are required, topOrders is kept, and delivery-history.fixtures.ts is extended with the new keys. That is one hand-written apps/web file, ~80 lines of fixture data, and nothing else breaks.

C. Breaking: topOrders is removed and replaced by topOrdersByCurrency. Breaks statistics-view-model.ts:142, delivery-stat-breakdowns.tsx:87-137 and the fixture, i.e. a real FE slice, which the caller excluded from this pass.
openDecisions.recommendation: B. Required keys keep the contract honest (backend/16:32) and the only casualty is one fixture file whose entire purpose is to satisfy the type. If the caller wants literally zero apps/web edits, take A and open a follow-up to tighten the keys during the FE pass. C should be rejected for this pass: the spec's own compatibility rule (backend/16:40) permits direct evolution only when all callers migrate in the same change, and the FE is explicitly not migrating here.
openDecisions.answer: ANSWERED 2026-08-20 (user): option B. New keys are REQUIRED, flat topOrders stays for now, and apps/web/src/features/delivery/components/delivery-history.fixtures.ts is extended so root pnpm typecheck stays green. No other apps/web file is touched. Removing topOrders is deferred to the frontend pass.

openDecisions.question: Does BookOrder gain an isFree column, or is the free-order invariant dropped in favour of an explicit totalAmount of 0?
openDecisions.specOffers: shared/02_CONTRACT_AND_INVARIANTS.md:22 and backend/01_financial_invariant_and_cancelled_scope.md:13 both state `isFree === true -> effective total = 0` as a mandatory rule, and backend/01:53-55 wants the canonical helper to return source "free".
openDecisions.codebaseMakesCheaper: Dropping it is free. There is no isFree column: apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma:358-378 lists id, userId, storeName, orderNumber, orderDate, currency, totalAmount, deliveryPrice, discount, note, createdAt, updatedAt and nothing else. Grep for "isFree" across apps/api/src, packages/shared/src and apps/web/src returns zero matches at dd144d45. Meanwhile a free order is already representable: OwnershipPriceSchema allows 0 (packages/shared/src/internal.ts:123-126, min OWNERSHIP_PRICE_MIN = 0), and the current resolver already returns an explicit 0 rather than falling through to item sums (order-statistics.ts:418-420). Adding the column costs a migration, two shared input schemas, a create path, an update path, a FE form field that is out of scope, and a codegen round.
options: A. Drop isFree. The canonical helper's source enum keeps "free" but derives it from an effective total that resolves to exactly 0, or drops "free" entirely and reports "manual".
B. Add isFree Boolean @default(false) to BookOrder with a migration, extend CreateBookOrderInputSchema and UpdateBookOrderInputSchema, and leave the FE form without the toggle until the FE pass.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. The invariant's product intent (a free order contributes 0, not an unknown) is already satisfied by an explicit total of 0, and B ships a column no UI can set in this pass.
openDecisions.answer: ANSWERED 2026-08-20 (user): drop isFree from the invariant. No column, no migration. A free order is an explicit totalAmount of 0; the resolver returns source 'manual' with effectiveTotal 0.

openDecisions.question: Does the query gain a period-preset field, or does previous_period only ever mean "equal-duration preceding range"?
openDecisions.specOffers: backend/02_statistics_period_and_comparison.md:14-33 defines distinct previous_period semantics for partial current month, full previous month, rolling N days, rolling N months and YTD. :35-38 then concedes that if the query carries only raw from/to, the implementation must support a mathematically equal-duration previous interval and "не вигадуй preset із недостатніх даних".
openDecisions.codebaseMakesCheaper: The query carries only raw from/to today (packages/shared/src/orders.ts:507,511; both isoDay().optional()), and the FE sends them as free-text ISO strings from two nuqs string parsers (apps/web/src/features/delivery/model/statistics-params.ts:23,27,57-58) with no preset concept anywhere. Equal-duration-only is therefore implementable with zero contract additions. Detecting a full calendar month from raw bounds is cheap and unambiguous (from is the 1st and to is the last day); detecting "partial current month" is also cheap (from is the 1st of the current month and to is today or later). Detecting "rolling 30 days" versus "custom 30-day range" from raw bounds is impossible.
options: A. Raw bounds only, with two safe inferences: a full calendar month maps to the full preceding month, a month-to-date window maps to the same day-range of the preceding month, and everything else maps to the equal-duration preceding range. No new query field.

B. Add an optional `periodPreset` enum to the query now, and have the backend honour it when present and fall back to A when absent. Costs one shared enum plus a codegen round; the FE cannot send it until the FE pass, so it is dead weight for now.
C. Full preset support with the preset as a required companion of compare. Rejected on sight: it would break the existing FE call at statistics-params.ts:47-59.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. It covers the two calendar cases the spec names most emphatically (backend/02:14-25) with no contract surface, and backend/02:38 explicitly forbids inventing the rest. Revisit B during the FE pass when a preset toolbar actually exists.
openDecisions.answer: ANSWERED 2026-08-20 (agent recommendation accepted): no new preset field. previous_period is derived from the raw from/to bounds, with full-calendar-month and month-to-date inferred from those bounds; rolling-N-days is not distinguishable from a custom range and is not faked.

openDecisions.question: Which stage names does the lifecycle block use?
openDecisions.specOffers: backend/06_lifecycle_status_distribution.md:26-30 suggests ordered / in_transit / ready_for_pickup / received / cancelled, and :41-43 sketches a response with ordered, inTransit, readyForPickup, received, cancelled, total. But :25 says "Adapt exact labels to canonical current domain" and :33 says "use existing computeBookOrderDerivedStatus for order mode". The two halves of the same file disagree.
openDecisions.codebaseMakesCheaper: Reusing the canonical helper is cheaper and is what README.md:31 demands. computeBookOrderDerivedStatus (apps/api/src/modules/delivery/domain/order-derived-status.ts:18-52) returns BookOrderDerivedStatus, whose six values are active, partially_shipped, shipped, partially_received, received, cancelled (packages/shared/src/orders.ts:59-66). The spec's five names are the ShipmentStatus enum instead (packages/shared/src/book-enums.ts:75-81: ordered, in_transit, ready_for_pickup, received, cancelled), which describes a shipment, not an order. The FE already renders badges for all six derived values (apps/web/src/features/delivery/model/statistics-view-model.ts:21-28).
options: A. Orders mode uses the six BookOrderDerivedStatus values verbatim; books mode uses an item-level set derived from the same vocabulary. Cancelled is the side branch in both.

B. Orders mode collapses the six derived values onto the spec's five funnel stages (active -> ordered, partially_shipped and shipped -> in_transit, partially_received and received -> received, plus ready_for_pickup pulled from the item's shipment status). A funnel reads better, but the collapse is a new precedence rule, which backend/06:34 forbids without extending the canonical helper.
C. Return both: the six raw counts plus a documented funnel projection over them.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. It satisfies the spec's own binding instruction (:25, :33-34) and never invents a precedence. If the funnel visual needs five bars, the collapse is presentation and belongs in the FE view-model, where reversing it later is a one-file change.
openDecisions.answer: ANSWERED 2026-08-20 (agent recommendation accepted): the six canonical BookOrderDerivedStatus values (active, partially_shipped, shipped, partially_received, received, cancelled). The five shipment-flavoured names in backend/06:26-30 are ShipmentStatus and are not used. Collapsing to a five-bar funnel is a frontend view-model concern.

openDecisions.question: Do active-money age and monthly budget get their own endpoints, or ride inside the statistics response?
openDecisions.specOffers: backend/10_active_money_age_buckets.md:46 says "Prefer separate read endpoint", with a fallback of keeping it inline if the API architecture prefers one endpoint. shared/04_PROPOSED_RESPONSE_SHAPES.md:59-88 sketches GET /api/delivery/orders/statistics/active-age. backend/13:86-89 says budget needs read plus upsert and to follow current route conventions. shared/04:7 separately says to prefer extending the existing statistics endpoint over many tiny per-widget endpoints.
openDecisions.codebaseMakesCheaper: Separate for both. The historical statistics read is date-bounded and capped (delivery-statistics.repository.ts:64-79); the age snapshot needs a different WHERE with no date bound, so inlining it means running two unrelated queries behind one route and then documenting that half the response ignores half the query — exactly the "misleading historical active money" backend/03:27 warns about. Budget has writes, so it cannot live inside a GET at all. The module already hosts four controllers (delivery.module.ts:25-30), so adding routes is mechanical. The route prefix is already right: BookOrdersController is @Controller("api/delivery/orders") (book-orders.controller.ts:38), so a @Get("statistics/active-age") sits next to the existing @Get("statistics") (:75).
options: A. Age snapshot as GET /api/delivery/orders/statistics/active-age on BookOrdersController; budget as its own BookBudgetsController with a read and an upsert.
B. Age snapshot inline in the statistics response, with a test proving from/to do not affect it; budget separate regardless.
C. Both inline where possible, with budget writes on a separate controller.
openDecisions.recommendation: A. Cleaner cache semantics, cheaper query, and it keeps the one place the spec explicitly fears (a snapshot silently reinterpreted as period data) impossible by construction.
openDecisions.answer: ANSWERED 2026-08-20 (agent recommendation accepted): separate endpoints. GET /api/delivery/orders/statistics/active-age for the snapshot, and its own budget routes.

openDecisions.question: Does the budget table reuse an existing settings model, and how many indexes does the migration add?
openDecisions.specOffers: backend/13_budget_persistence_and_api.md:16-32 sketches a dedicated model with a unique on userId + currency + validFromMonth and "no overlapping active intervals per user/currency". :42 says to reuse a generic user-settings model only if the semantics fit cleanly. backend/15:38 asks to check budget indexes.
openDecisions.codebaseMakesCheaper: A new table. The only per-user settings model is UserProfileSettings (apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma:660-683): one row per user (userId is @unique at :662) holding seventeen flat scalar preference columns. It cannot express a per-currency versioned history without either a JSON blob or three more nullable columns plus month bounds, which is precisely the overloading :42 forbids. On indexes, @@unique([userId, currency, validFromMonth]) is expressible in Prisma and its leading columns already serve every read, so no extra plain index is warranted. The open question is only whether to also enforce "at most one open version per user and currency" in the database.
options: A. New table, one Prisma @@unique, no raw SQL. The one-open-version rule is enforced only by the service inside its transaction (T61). Simplest migration; a concurrent double-write could in principle leave two open versions.

B. New table, one Prisma @@unique plus a hand-written partial unique index (WHERE valid_to_month IS NULL). Makes the invariant a database fact. Costs a raw SQL block in the migration and a twelfth entry in apps/api/src/core/database/raw-sql-indexes.test.ts, whose list currently holds exactly eleven (:35-45), and permanently enlarges the CLAUDE.md §6 strip-trap surface.
C. Overload UserProfileSettings with budget columns. Rejected.
openDecisions.recommendation: B. This repo already treats one-active-X as a database invariant in five places (book_order_items_active_book_idx, book_loans_active_book_idx, reading_goals_active_list_idx and two more), and a budget row is money. The cost is one guard-test line. Choose A only if you want the migration to stay pure Prisma output.
openDecisions.answer: ANSWERED 2026-08-20 (user): new dedicated table (UserProfileSettings cannot hold versioned per-currency money). Composite unique (userId, currency, validFromMonth) via Prisma PLUS a raw-SQL partial unique index WHERE valid_to_month IS NULL enforcing one open version per user+currency, registered as the 12th entry in apps/api/src/core/database/raw-sql-indexes.test.ts.

openDecisions.question: Does the effective-total invariant change any create or update validation that exists today?
openDecisions.specOffers: shared/02_CONTRACT_AND_INVARIANTS.md:32-34 calls this "a deliberate domain-contract change" and demands an audit of all create/update forms, DTOs, tests, statistics and imports/exports. backend/01:78 requires "the old mismatch invariant removed/adapted everywhere".
openDecisions.codebaseMakesCheaper: Nothing to change. CreateBookOrderInputSchema (packages/shared/src/orders.ts:194-209) carries four refinements — unique ordered books, shipments only carry ordered books, each book ships once, expected delivery not before order date — and none compares totalAmount to the item subtotal. UpdateBookOrderInputSchema (:213-222) carries no refinement at all. The named symbols resolveOrderFinancials, validateOrderFinancials and OrderTotalSource do not exist anywhere in the repo. The only effective-total logic is the private resolveOrderAmount (apps/api/src/modules/delivery/domain/order-statistics.ts:411-424), which is statistics-only and throws nothing.
options: A. Treat the removal requirement as already satisfied and spend the budget on a regression test proving a mismatched manual total is accepted (T11).
B. Search harder for a hidden mismatch rule before implementing, on the assumption the spec author saw one on a different branch.
openDecisions.recommendation: A, with one caveat the caller should confirm: the spec was written against something. If it was written against an unmerged branch or a planned design rather than dev, the real risk is not a removal we skipped but a create/update behaviour the author intends to ADD (delivery and discount participating in a validated total). Confirm whether the spec author expected order creation to start validating totals; if yes, that is new work with no task here.
openDecisions.answer: ANSWERED 2026-08-20 (user): nothing changes on the write path. Order create/update keep accepting totalAmount as given. The invariant lives on the read path only; the difference between the explicit total and subtotal + delivery - discount surfaces as a derived reconciliation adjustment used by landed-cost allocation.

openDecisions.question: Where do the new shared statistics contracts live?
openDecisions.specOffers: backend/16_shared_contracts_and_openapi.md:6 says consolidate all new shapes in packages/shared; shared/04:1-3 says these are semantic shapes, not permission to bypass existing naming conventions.
openDecisions.codebaseMakesCheaper: Splitting. packages/shared/src/orders.ts is already 574 lines and holds the whole delivery contract; this spec adds roughly a dozen more schema families. The barrel (packages/shared/src/index.ts) re-exports every file with `export * from`, so a consumer's `import { X } from "@app/shared"` is unaffected by which file X lives in — moving or adding a file is invisible to all 1719 generated FE files and to every hand-written import.
options: A. New file packages/shared/src/order-statistics.ts for everything new, leaving the four existing statistics schemas where they are in orders.ts. Two files describe statistics.

B. New file plus move the four existing statistics schemas into it. One concern per file (CLAUDE.md §8.10), invisible to consumers thanks to the barrel, but the diff touches lines apps/web reads and makes D1's blast radius harder to eyeball in review.
C. Everything into orders.ts, taking it past 900 lines.
openDecisions.recommendation: A for this pass, B as a follow-up once the contract has settled. Keeping the moved-code diff out of the same commit as the contract change is what makes the D1 review tractable.
openDecisions.answer: ANSWERED 2026-08-20 (agent recommendation accepted): new schemas go in packages/shared/src/order-statistics.ts. The four existing statistics schemas stay in orders.ts this pass.
